text: Here's a fact that genuinely catches people off guard: Data Factory only stores pipeline run history for forty-five days. The Monitor hub is built for recent troubleshooting, not as a permanent audit trail. If you need to answer how a pipeline's failure rate trended over the last six months, the Monitor hub alone simply can't answer that.

The fix is a diagnostic setting that streams Data Factory's resource logs to a Log Analytics workspace, retained on your own terms and queryable with real code. Check only the categories you actually need — ActivityRuns, PipelineRuns, TriggerRuns for nearly every factory, and skip every SSIS category entirely if you don't use SSIS at all.

The destination table setting offers two real modes. Azure diagnostics dumps every category into one shared table, which can hit Azure's five-hundred column limit fast once multiple services write into it. Resource specific gives each category its own dedicated table instead — ADFPipelineRun, ADFActivityRun — and it's Microsoft's own recommended default.

Once logs are flowing, allowing up to fifteen minutes for a new event to actually appear, you query them with the Kusto Query Language. Filter out FailureType not equal UserError to exclude failures caused by your own pipeline configuration, surfacing genuine system-level reliability issues instead — a pattern worth remembering for nearly every query you'll write against this data.

That closes out Chapter Eight: the Monitor hub, alerts and retry policies, real error handling patterns, and now genuine long-term logging through Log Analytics. Next, Chapter Nine: Fabric Data Factory — the forward-looking evolution of nearly everything you've built across this entire course so far.
